claim: The rescaled differential system bounds the outer-disk maximum by its state at the center. Cauchy estimates bound that state by the inner-disk maximum and give the two-disk growth estimate. The public proof context is Turan.lemma_fourteen.

The public harmonic disk Harnack inequality gives the two sharp factors (R∓d)/(R±d) for nonnegative boundary data and harmonicity with continuous boundary values. The derivative proof uses a logarithmic branch and its own Schwarz-transform Harnack estimate with 9/5 at d/R≤2/7.

For holomorphic g with Re g≥0 on B(z₀,R), R>0, the direct public theorem gives ‖g⁽ˡ⁾(z₀)‖≤2·l!·Re g(z₀)/Rˡ for every l≥1. In the Ω-rescaled disk R=7 for D=Ω⁻¹∂. Lemma 14 itself uses the Schwarz transform and the first four exponential jets to prove ‖F⁽ˡ⁾/F‖≤(11Ω)ˡ for 1≤l≤4.

New direct proof for both ordered choices (j,j′)=(n,m),(m,n), 2≤n<m and every z with P_nm(z)≠0. With t=(E_*+j′)F the coefficients are (1−Q_j) and −Q_j/j and the left side is (j′−j)β_j H_j(z). Rescaling the coefficients gives the printed ψ_j form. F(z)≠0 is needed only for the subsequent division by F.
For 2≤n<m the sole zero of P_nm(z)=1+2(1−1/n)(1−1/m)z is the real point −1/[2(1−1/n)(1−1/m)], so P_nm is nonzero at every nonreal z.

place: Upper-index identity, value of the twice-filtered affine denominator
claim: In the ordered proof with t=(E_*+j′)F, hden gives t(z)+(E_*t)(z)/j=j′[1+2(1−1/j)(1−1/j′)z]. This is the printed twice-filtered affine value with j′ cleared. The calculation uses the mode expansions before the quotient cancellation.

The mode expansions for E_*F and E_*²F involve derivatives only through order four. The new identity gives the printed exact Q_j at P_nm≠0. On the two lines the proof of Lemma 15 divides by F and uses a cancelling q to estimate the same two modes.

claim: For m≥450, m/2≤n<m, either ordering (j,j′) of (n,m), and |Im z|=7/11, the actual Q_j=P_j′/P_nm satisfies Q_j−1=z/[(j−1)(z−x_*)] and |Q_j−1|<2.59/j<5/j, where x_* is the real zero of P_nm.

J2 C11 checks the scalar margin below 5 using j≥225 and λ≥449/450. The exact Q_j occurs in the public projection. The boundary theorem bounds its constructed witness by the weak 5/j endpoint. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (J2).

J2 C12 checks 322.5/900+(46/45)4067<4200. Independently the line-mode proof carries out this comparison with a weak 4200 endpoint in the universal line estimate. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (J2).
Removing the weight and a factor for each nearby real zero gives ‖U_j(w₀)‖≤25000 m²/(j(m−n)) times the specified node product, for both modes. The public proof context is Turan.lemma_sixteen.
The weight is nonzero on the closed strip. Lean works with its constant multiple (√(2m)−4iz)⁴ and bounds the norm of its affine base below by 1. The public proof context is Turan.lemma_sixteen.

claim: For real s and y_*=7/11, tanh(π(z−s)/(4y_*)) maps |Im z|<y_* onto the open unit disk, has modulus one on both boundary lines, and has s as its only zero in the closed strip.

The exponential form of the tanh factor has modulus one on the boundary, vanishes at s only within the strip, and can be removed at a zero of a holomorphic function. On the real axis it equals the printed real tanh. The public proof context is Turan.lemma_sixteen.

The strip maximum bound after division holds for a finite set of distinct real zeros. The application takes all real Hermite roots in [−7/2,5/2] and evaluates their product at w₀. The public proof context is Turan.lemma_sixteen.

The node-product gain exceeds 0.608√(2j−11.25)−0.315. The paper's cited Lemma 17 defines the gain as +∞ for a central zero. Lean encodes this by a disjunction, handling a zero at w₀ separately. The public proof context is Turan.large_upper_index_gap.

For α=11π/28, ω(v)=log coth(αv) is strictly convex and strictly decreasing on v>0. For the noncentral Hermite node pairs this gives the midpoint lower bound for the full weight before truncation.

J2 C15–C18 check the worst mesh and the numerical coefficient and subtraction bounds 0.608 and 0.315. The node-product theorem is separately proved in Lean. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (J2).

For both j=n and j=m, log(50000 m²/(j(m−n)))<0.608√(2j−11.25)−0.315 throughout the upper-index range. Lean proves the actual inequality by splitting at 2m/3 and 19m/20. The public proof context is Turan.large_upper_index_gap.

For each real m≥450 the difference D_m(n) at j=n is strictly concave on [m/2,m−1], with minimum equal to the smaller endpoint value. The right-hand logarithm equals log 200000 at m/2 and is ≤log(50200m) at m−1.

At m=450 the left endpoint margin exceeds 0.214 and the right endpoint lower bound exceeds 0.857. The left margin and the right lower bound both have positive derivative and strictly increase on real m≥450, so both endpoint comparisons persist.
J2 C24 verifies that the quadratic discriminant in the right-endpoint derivative comparison is negative, by exact rational arithmetic. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (J2).

The product and scalar comparisons give both mode norms strictly below 1/2, also when a node is exactly at w₀. Their sum equals 1, contradicting the triangle inequality. The public proof context is Turan.large_upper_index_gap.

Passing between normalized Hermites, H_j and the circle modes 128^j H_j rescales the two free coefficients. The Giroux row rounds the square roots outward, including sqrt(3) ≤ 1733/1000.
Numerical search, the description of the four methods and the pointer to READ_FIRST are provenance and navigation. The arithmetic checks are listed individually.

place: Section 4, pointwise multiplicity in the dominant-coefficient test
claim: In the normalized variable v, let f have a global power-series expansion with coefficients A_k. If ℓ ≥ 1 and the sum of |A_k| off ℓ is strictly below |A_ℓ|, dominant_entire_term supplies a multiset of cardinality ℓ. Its count at v is analyticOrderAt f v for |v| < 1 and zero outside. dominant_polynomial_term gives the polynomial version. The separate closed-box comparison is the following row.

claim: A common lower bound for one coefficient that exceeds a summable majorant of all other coefficients gives the exact zero count for each parameter.

For a real center and radius the first coefficient of the scaled Hermite expansion equals its real pivot. The sum of the remaining absolute coefficients bounds the remainder on the unit circle. The public proof context is Turan.circle_certificate_gap.

claim: Zero-freeness on the open disk gives the joint first-coefficient inequality for the two modes under the stated phase and weight conditions.

The exponential factor preserves zeros. Dividing by its nonzero value at the center normalizes the pivot, and the weighted certificate row bounds the affine term and the two remainders. The public proof context is Turan.circle_certificate_gap.

For δ=ρ φ′_j(ξ), the remainder after δv on the disk is at most cosh(sqrt Q_j) abs(φ_j(ξ)) + (sinh(sqrt Q_j)/sqrt Q_j − 1) abs(δ). Lean proves the oscillator equation and this bound by differential comparison along radii. The public proof context is Turan.circle_certificate_gap.

place: Section 4, Giroux attribution in the general orthogonal setting
claim: Giroux, Estimates for the imaginary parts of the zeros of a polynomial, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 44 (1974), 61–67, quoted from Schmeisser, Math. Balkanica (N.S.) 16 (2002), Theorem B, supplies the general orthogonal-expansion estimate. Lean proves the Hermite specialization independently and assumes no general Giroux theorem.

The paper quotes Giroux through Theorem B of Schmeisser (2002) for the root-height sum. Lean proves the normalized Hermite expansion bound with multiplicities and arbitrary nonzero leading coefficient from a rank-one Jacobi perturbation. The sparse lower coefficients are 1, sqrt(2), a, with squared norms summing to 3+abs(a)². The public proof context is Turan.circle_certificate_gap.

A3 runs both programs on the 126 replacement 87/100 circle systems. The archive guide identifies 60 replacements using a Giroux row. The Hermite inequality and its conversion into a cut are proved in Lean. A3 verifies the frozen replacement systems. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (A3).

Each of the m roots for b ≠ 0 has height ≥ 87/100 under strip avoidance. Bounding sqrt(3+abs(a)²) by sqrt(3)+abs(a) gives (87/100)sqrt(2m) abs(b) ≤ sqrt(3)+abs(a), also for b=0. The public proof context is Turan.circle_certificate_gap.

The sign of Re(a conjugate(b)) selects the sector. Valid rows force their cuts at both nonnegative coefficient magnitudes, contradicting certified infeasibility and giving the strict strip root. Fourier–Motzkin elimination producing infeasibility is external. The public proof context is Turan.circle_certificate_gap.

The zero when both coefficients vanish is −1/2. Otherwise division by the larger rescaled coefficient gives either order, abs(χ) ≤ 1 and unrestricted κ. Conjugating χ, κ and the zero reduces to Im χ ≥ 0. The public proof context is Turan.ratio_certificate_gap.

place: Section 4, class (b), cap from the first disk
claim: The public cap assumes a zero-free strip and bounds |κ| by (mass(P)+|χ| mass(Q))/(2ρ). Its proof obtains a zero in the first open disk about −1/2 whenever the cap fails. This localized witness is the disk argument used in the paper.

place: Section 4, class (b), root from two disks
claim: The affine cap and the checked positive-order pivot through order ten force a zero on the interior of the first or second disk, including after removal of the nonvanishing Gaussian. Both chart orders give the strict strip result. The public proof context is Turan.ratio_certificate_gap. The high-disk proof uses circle_comparison for existence. The separate general entire-function multiplicity count is dominant_entire_term.
B1 checks the 411 earlier chart pairs with 5,688 leaf disks. R00 checks the retained radii for the 87/100 application. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (B1).

B3 checks the 18 new pairs on all 132 leaves of their ratio charts. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (B3).

place: Section 4, class (b), Taylor coefficients through order ten
claim: The primary ratio verifier generates the retained Gaussian Taylor coefficients by the differential recurrence. B2 independently uses direct Gaussian convolution, the representation proved in Lean by mode_series. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (B1, B2, B3).

On the doubled disk the oscillator bounds the mode. Cauchy bounds each coefficient of order l by M/2^l, giving the tail from order eleven bounded by M/1024 on the unit circle. The public proof context is Turan.ratio_certificate_gap.

A real nonzero multiple of H_n gives the normalized low mode. Rescaling by the larger coefficient and conjugating when necessary reduces the pencil to its two indicated forms with abs(ϑ) ≤ 1 and Im ϑ ≥ 0, for arbitrary high coefficient. The public proof context is Turan.transfer_certificate_gap.

For each normalized parameter, the strict product comparison either gives outer dominance at the high Hermite zero or inner dominance of the low pivot over the perturbation. This proves the open-strip conclusion for all high coefficients. The public proof context is Turan.transfer_certificate_gap. This implication uses the paired coefficient-mass test. The separate uniform perturbation theorem takes UniformTransferCheck.

C1 checks 759 singleton leaves across n=2,…,7 with an inner disk inside the 87/100 strip and abs(z) ≤ 5/4, and a positive-order pivot margin exceeding 1/64. The six leaf counts are 112, 136, 172, 100, 148, 91. In Lean, UniformTransferCheck expresses the resulting pointwise existence of the disk and margin on the full closed parameter rectangle in both charts. The public perturbation theorem takes this predicate as a hypothesis. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (C1).

claim: For n=2,…,7, either chart order and |Re θ| ≤ 1, 0 ≤ Im θ ≤ 1, UniformTransferCheck supplies a positive-order margin > 1/64. A single disk with |w|+r ≤ 5/4 and |Im w|+r < 87/100 works for every polynomial g satisfying |g(z)| < 1/64 throughout |z| ≤ 5/4. The proof applies circle_comparison and obtains a zero of F₀+g in the open disk. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (C1).
The outer circle gives a positive endpoint minimum for the high mode and bounds the perturbation coefficient by the actual maximum of the pencil norm divided by that minimum.

C1 verifies the common 1/64 perturbation test for the 2,524 pairs starting at upper degrees 24,26,29,30,33,34 for n=2,…,7 respectively, through 449. Both integer and PARI programs check the uniform data. The high-mode bound is an archive calculation. The Lean perturbation theorem gives the zero once the required uniform smallness and low-mode check are supplied. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (C1).

C1 verifies 75 further pairs on 3,171 dyadic leaves, down to m=16,18,14,17,17,19 respectively. The local test compares the two disk masses and the local pivot margin directly. A common 1/64 bound for the local leaves is not the tested predicate. The corresponding public implication uses TransferCertificate n m. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (C1).

place: Section 4, low-index remainder assigned to winding
claim: The two C1 lists leave 58 admissible pairs with n ≤ 7. In R00’s winding lists, 49 belong to the 265-pair archive and nine to the quadratic archive. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (R00, C1).

claim: The winding normalizations are real nonzero Hermite multiples. The same two chart orders, conjugation and affine circle bound on abs(κ) apply with these scales. The public proof context is Turan.winding_certificate_gap.

For a fixed polynomial and an edge passing its coefficient test, the polynomial image of the entire segment lies in the disk of radius abs(c) about c, excluding zero. The checked nominal endpoints are also in this disk. The public proof context is Turan.winding_certificate_gap. The same edge_disk estimate is used by the compact-convex localization proof.

The mathematical implication from these edge enclosures and a positive tally to a zero in their rectangle is proved in Lean. Recorded replay evidence comes from frozen v0.93 (D1).

claim: Summing continuous local changes of argument along the polynomial edges gives exactly 2π times the signed crossings of the nominal polygon, including when roots lie inside the polygon.

claim: The two equal divided differences give equal normalized family values, their endpoint quotient and the corresponding quotient product over all roots with multiplicity.

For every nonreal z, the integral defining intervalAngle equals arg(r−z)−arg(l−z) as real numbers. The proof differentiates the principal argument along the slit plane and applies the fundamental theorem of calculus. For l<r the integrand has the sign of Im z, and the two endpoint rays lie in the same open half-plane. The absolute change is their subtended angle.

place: Section 4, sum and parity for general F
claim: A continuous argument along the real axis increases by the sum of the signed angles over all roots with multiplicity. At equal nodes the increment is an even or odd multiple of π according to their signs.

place: Section 4, exact odd or even sum of integrated root angles
claim: For any complex polynomial p with no real zeros, l<r distinct from −1/2, and p(r)/p(l)=(2r+1)/(2l+1), the sum of intervalAngle l r over p.roots with multiplicity is (2k+1)π when l<−1/2<r and 2kπ otherwise, for some integer k. The proof factors p, adds phases modulo 2π, then uses the sign of the real quotient to obtain this equality in ℝ.

For every l<r and nonreal z=x+iy, with μ=(l+r)/2 and s=(r−l)/2, cot |intervalAngle l r z| = ((x−μ)²+y²−s²)/(2|y|s). The proof covers acute, right and obtuse subtended angles without a sign assumption on the numerator.

All coefficient pairs have height at most Im z_* for the unique upper zero of 12z⁴+16z³+12z²−3. The two maximizing conjugate quartics have roots z_*,z_*,z_*,−3z_* or their conjugates.
